CITY  OF  ALHAMBRA

  REGULARMEETING OF THE
  ALHAMBRA HOUSING AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT
  CITIZEN ADVISORY COMMITTEE

The Regular Meeting of the Alhambra Housing and Community Development Citizen
Advisory (HCDA) Committee will be held on Tuesday, February 2, 2021, commencing
at 7:00 p.m. via teleconference and video conference.

  CORONAVIRUS (COVID-19) ADVISORY NOTICE

Consistent with Executive Orders No. N-29-20 and No. N-35-20 from the Executive
Department of the State of California and the County of Los Angeles Department of Public
Health Safer At Home Order, the Alhambra Housing and Community Development
Citizen Advisory Committee meeting will not be physically open to the public and the
meeting will take place via teleconference and video conference.

To watch and listen to the meeting: To maximize public safety while still maintaining
transparency and public access, members of the public can participate by using Zoom
Meeting as follows:

Zoom direct link:

https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82123937038?pwd=aGo3eVJzYk8rMkhOZGhOQ1g4RnNMZz09

Webinar ID: 821 2393 7038

Passcode: 389133

Or by telephone by dialing: 1-833-548-0276 (Toll Free) or 1-833-548-0282 (Toll Free) or
1-877-853-5257 (Toll Free) or 1-888-475-4499 (Toll Free)

Webinar ID: 821 2393 7038 and Passcode: 389133

Please Note: All members of the public calling or logging into the meeting will be muted
so that the meeting can proceed. For those wishing to speak on an agenda item, please
email Matthew Cuevas at mcuevas@cityofalhambra.org by 5:00 p.m. prior to the meeting
with the item number you wish to speak on and the phone number you will use when
calling or the name you will use when logging into the meeting. You should then call or
log into the meeting at least 5 minutes prior to its start time. Staff will unmute you and
announce you when it is your time to speak. You will have five minutes to speak, unless
that time is adjusted by the meeting Chair. Given the challenges of teleconference and
video conference meetings, all participants are encouraged to email their comments
prior to the beginning of the meeting.
 Comments can be emailed to the Matthew Cuevas at mcuevas@cityofalhambra.org by no
later than 5:00 p.m. on February 2, 2021 to ensure there is sufficient time to print the
emails prior to the beginning of the meeting. Comments will then be read into the record,
with a maximum allowance of 5 minutes per individual comment, subject to the Chair’s
discretion. If a comment is received after 5:00 p.m. but before the conclusion of the
meeting based upon its time stamp, the comment will still be included as a part of the
record of the meeting but will not be read into the record.

An agenda of the regular meeting is attached hereto incorporated herein by reference and
made a part hereof as though fully set forth herein.
   AGENDA
  REGULAR MEETING
HOUSING AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT CITIZEN ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  TUESDAY, FEBRURARY 2, 2021 AT 7:00 P.M.

1. ROLL CALL:
  Bill Vallejos, Chair  Mark Lee, Vice Chair
  Bonita Sharma-Ngan  Andrea Giese
  Marc Tousignant  Marcos Sayon
  Maria Conchita Bañuelos  Yvette Cardenas

2. MINUTES
  Approval of the minutes for the Regular Meeting of October 6, 2020.

3. PROGRESS REPORTS
  Attached for the Committee’s review are copies of the Progress Reports for those programs
  utilizing Community Development Block Grant and HOME Funds. All figures indicate the
  progress made and services rendered to date for FY 2020-2021.
   Parks and Recreation - Case Management
   73 Case Management clients were served.
   0 Volunteer Hours of assistance were donated to the program.
   Community Development - Code Enforcement
   The Code Enforcement Division investigated a total of 277 complaints.
   30 were identified as confirmed complaints as stand-alone Health & Safety Issues.
   Code Enforcement staff referred 81 to the Housing Department programs.
   Community Development - Fair Housing
   The Housing Rights Center served approx. 24 clients.
   A variety of issues were discussed, including: evictions, security deposits, rent
  increases, repairs, contract questions, etc.
   Community Development - Housing Programs
   First-Time Home Buyer - HOME: 15 searching for a home, 0 escrow closed.
   HOME Major Rehabilitation: 2 in process, 1 completed.
   CDBG Minor Rehabilitation: 2 in process, 1 completed.

  Recommended Action
  Receive and file these informational reports.

4. 2021-2022 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN PROGRAM PREPARATION AND STUDY
  SESSION
  Each year, in preparation for the Annual Action Plan, staff presents the current and possible
  new programs to receive Community Development Block Grant or HOME funds in the
  coming program year. This gives the Housing and Community Development Act Citizen's
  Advisory Committee and the community an opportunity to see the programs offered by the
  City of Alhambra and preview any new or proposed projects/programs being considered for
  funding.
   Recommended Action
  No recommended action required. This is a study session to review requirements and submit
  considerations in preparation of the DRAFT 2021-2022 Annual Action Plan.

5. COMMENTS FROM THE AUDIENCE
  Discussion from the public of any item not specified on the agenda. Comments must pertain
  to the business of the HCDA Citizen Advisory Committee. Public comments pertaining to
  the HCDA Committee’s business are welcome. Kindly limit all oral communications to five
  (5) minutes. Please complete the blue speaker card prior to the meeting and submit it to the
  Committee’s secretary.

6. COMMENTS AND CONCERNS FROM THE COMMITTEE
  Discussion from the Committee Members of any item(s) not specified on the agenda. Items
  discussed must pertain to the business of the HCDA Citizen Advisory Committee.

7. ADJOURNMENT

 Copies of the staff report or other written documentation relating to each item of business described herein
 above are on file in the office of Management Services, Alhambra City Hall, 111 S. First Street, Alhambra,
 CA, and are available for public inspection during regular office hours: 7:00 A.M. to 12:00 P.M., Monday
 through Thursday.
 Should any person have a question concerning any of the above agenda items prior to the meeting described
 herein, he or she may contact Mr. Matthew Cuevas, Management Analyst, either in person, at the
 Management Services Department located at City Hall, or call via telephone at (626) 570-5011, during
 regular business hours.

 Americans with Disabilities Act: If you require special assistance to participate in any City meeting, please
 contact the City Clerk's Office (626) 570-5090. Notification of at least 72 hours prior to the meeting will
 enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to this meeting.

 4. PRESENTATION FROM CITY’S HOMELESS OUTREACH PROVIDER – LOS
  ANGELES CENTERS FOR ALCOHOL AND DRUG ABUSE (L.A. CADA)
  Assistant City Manager Garcia introduced the City’s new homeless outreach provider L.A.
  CADA to the Committee.

  Bill Tarkanian, Director of Program Development, introduced himself and the additional team
  members, Mary Kemp, Virginia Valencia and Wayne Smith who all work on homeless
  outreach issues in the City.

  Housing Navigator Smith introduced himself and his qualifications to the HCDA Committee.
  He touched on the outreach services he provides in Alhambra by engaging clients daily.
  Housing Navigator Smith mentioned his approach is to build rapport with the clients and meet
  them where they are at. He also conducts assessments on clients through the Coordinated Entry
  System (CES) and Clarity to evaluate each client’s vulnerability to homelessness, as well as
  Project Room Key referrals and trying to connect clients to as many resources as possible.

  Housing Navigator Valencia introduced herself and her qualifications in assisting clients. She
  spoke about the population in Alhambra and engaging individuals dealing with substance
  abuse and others dealing with additional barriers such as mental health. Housing Navigator
  Valencia spoke about one recent example where she and Housing Navigator Smith assisted a
  client into the Coordinated Entry System (CES). She mentioned the client had been homeless
  since 2005 and had numerous medical and mental health issues. Housing Navigators Valencia
  and Smith were able to get this client into CES to streamline his housing match. She also
  discussed some of the lessons she has learned realizing that many of the clients they engage do
  not want services; however, they continue to engage and build trust with those individuals.

  Clinical Care Coordinator Kemp introduced herself and her qualifications. She spoke about
  working with the community and residents in the community and encountering different and
  complex situations daily. She spoke about working with the Alhambra Police Department and
  how they have been exemplary in coordinating with L.A. CADA daily on keeping track,
  navigating and assisting clients. Clinical Care Coordinator Kemp stated she found the daily
  communications and collaboration very effective since things change hourly.

  Housing Navigator Valencia shared a success story with a SUD (substance use disorder) client.
  Housing Navigator Smith talked about visiting the client after treatment and how the client
  was looking forward to going to a new facility in South Gate and finding employment. Housing
  Navigator Valencia mentioned the client was outreached at an abandoned lot at Fremont and
  Orange and was living in a storage bin and is now sober and starting his new life.

  Chair Vallejos inquired if any Committee members had any questions.

  Committee Member Sharma-Ngan thanked L.A. CADA for the work they do and asked how
  people get services, is it through referrals from the police department or referrals through
  community members.

  Housing Navigator Valencia answered they conduct outreach daily and spend a certain number
  of hours driving around Alhambra to engage any individual on the street. She also responded
  there are times the police department will contact them after an individual has been arrested
  but is asking for their services. Housing Navigator Valencia also stated that at times they
  receive calls from members of the community.
  Page 2 of 4
   Committee Member Tousignant inquired about the Point in Time Count and numbers gone
  down by a third, was wondering what might have been responsible for the drop? In addition,
  the split between sheltered and unsheltered individuals, where are the sheltered individuals
  being placed?

  Director Tarkanian provided a response to the second part of the question. He spoke about the
  City moving away from paying for motel vouchers for homeless individuals. In the first month,
  L.A. CADA targeted about eight to ten people who had been on vouchers for six months or
  longer. L.A. CADA has been able to resolve all of those and the City is no longer paying for
  those. In regards to housing, he spoke about the 185 transitional housing beds L.A. CADA has
  available at facilities in Pasadena/Altadena, unincorporated East Los Angeles, South Gate, and
  Long Beach; and there are dedicated beds for individuals from Alhambra in South Gate,
  Pasadena/Altadena and in East Los Angeles on an emergency basis. In addition, there are a
  couple of beds available at a shelter in Whittier. He also mentioned there are 75 residential
  beds for individuals who have an SUD (substance use disorder) problem and are able to house
  those individuals for a 60 to a 120-day residential stay. Director Tarkanian also mentioned
  there will be an additional 16 beds for mental health services that will be coming on-line on
  December 1.

  Committee Member Tousignant inquired for the staff conducting the street outreach, what the
  biggest barrier they are seeing to address housing and supportive services, and what does the
  City need to be aware of and responding to make L.A. CADA’s job easier?

  Director Tarkanian noted that one of the issues was change in the law that made drug
  possession cases misdemeanor’s and cite and releases. He noted they have been working with
  police departments to consider taking these individuals into custody for at least one night, and
  when they appear in court to be able to get their attention to consider treatment. He noted it
  allows L.A. CADA to screen them in court and they have been successful doing this approach
  in Long Beach and feel it can be part of the solution here. Director Tarkanian also responded
  there are a myriad of obstacles and a lot are mental health related, where one day the person is
  open to receiving services and the next day they are not.

  Chair Vallejos asked if there were any other question from Committee Members.

  Committee Member Tousignant indicated he would follow up offline with additional questions
  he had. He thanked L.A. CADA for the work they are doing and trying to help the homeless
  neighbors in Alhambra. Committee Member Tousignant stated he had some more questions
  and if L.A. CADA was open to more ways the City could help them do the job they are doing;
  we would welcome that opportunity.

  Director Tarkanian thanked Committee Member Tousignant for his comments and support.

  Chair Vallejos also thanked L.A. CADA for their efforts and welcomed them aboard, and for
  presenting tonight.

  Committee Action:
  By order of the Chair, the presentation was received and filed.
